about.h1: The Quran is Allah’s guidance for humanity, showing a clear way to live with faith, justice, mercy, and accountability.
about.lede: AskQuran helps people reach Quranic guidance clearly, directly, and with proper context — never an invented answer, always the source text.
about.whyHead: The Quran is guidance for human life
about.whyP1: It speaks to the heart, the family, society, business, justice, mercy, accountability, and the relationship between a person and Allah. It teaches people how to worship, how to deal with others, how to protect the rights of parents, spouses, children, relatives, orphans, the poor, and the vulnerable — and how to live with honesty, patience, dignity, and responsibility.
about.whyP2: It gives clear guidance on many matters people face in daily life: inheritance, marriage, divorce, wealth, trade, debt, charity, oppression, forgiveness, repentance, and personal conduct. It tells the stories of prophets and earlier nations — not only as history, but as lessons about belief, arrogance, injustice, corruption, morality, and the consequences of human choices.
about.beliefLead: AskQuran is built around this belief:
about.beliefHi: people should be able to reach Quranic guidance clearly, directly, and with proper context.
about.whatP1: When someone asks a life-related question, AskQuran searches the available Quran data and returns relevant Quran references — with the original Arabic ayah, a selected translation, surrounding ayah context, and tafsir where available.
about.inc1s: The Quran ayah in its original Arabic
about.inc4s: The verses immediately before and after
about.inc6s: Every text traced to its origin
about.lineHead: It points to the source — it does not speak for it
about.does1: Search indexed Quran data and return relevant references
about.does2: Quote the source text directly and in full context
about.does3: Help people study the relevant passages with clarity
about.does4: Say so plainly when no clear source-backed reference is found
about.doesNot1: Generate religious opinions, fatwas, or personal interpretations
about.doesNot3: Alter translations or tafsir in any way
about.doesNot4: Invent an answer or stretch relevance to fill a gap
about.sensitiveHead: Topic labels are a navigation layer — nothing more
about.sensitiveP1: For sensitive subjects such as inheritance, divorce, women's rights, family disputes, property, or social conduct, AskQuran uses reviewed topic metadata to connect common questions with relevant Quran passages.
about.noteH3: These labels are only a way to navigate
about.noteP: They are not Quran text, not tafsir, and not religious rulings. They must be reviewed before being used publicly, and they are kept clearly separate from the source text at every step.
about.commitHead: Four things we will always do
about.pledge1s: The source ayah is kept exactly as revealed, untouched.
about.pledge2s: Presented as written by their named authors.
about.pledge3s: Source text and topic labels never blur together.
about.pledge4s: No clear reference? We say so, rather than stretch.

facts.animal.dogN: Includes the dog of the companions of the cave.
facts.animal.wolfN: Mentioned in the account of Yusuf.
facts.animal.elephantN: Referenced in the account of the companions of the elephant.
facts.animal.snakeN: Different terms are used; some occur in the account of Musa's staff.
facts.animal.birdN: General references to birds across several contexts.
facts.animal.hoopoeN: Mentioned in the account of Sulayman.
facts.animal.crowN: Mentioned in the account of the two sons of Adam.
facts.animal.fishWhaleN: Includes the fish associated with Musa's journey and Yunus. Identification as fish or whale varies by translation.
facts.animal.beeN: Surah An-Nahl is named after the bee.
facts.animal.antN: Mentioned in the valley of the ants in the account of Sulayman.
facts.animal.spiderN: Referenced in a parable about frail reliance.
facts.animal.flyN: Mentioned in a parable about the powerlessness of false objects of worship.
facts.animal.mosquitoN: Mentioned as an example Allah may use, however small.
facts.animal.locustN: Mentioned among the signs sent to Pharaoh's people, and at the gathering.

relations.i.actJustly.label: The Quran commands being upholders of justice even toward those you dislike.
relations.i.noCompulsion.title: No Compulsion in Religion
relations.i.noCompulsion.label: The Quran declares there is no compulsion in religion.
relations.i.debateBest.title: Debate in the Best Way
relations.i.debateBest.label: The Quran commands inviting to Allah's way with wisdom and good argument.
relations.i.doNotAid.title: Do Not Aid Those Who Fight You
relations.i.doNotAid.label: The Quran forbids taking as allies those who fight believers and expel them.
relations.i.honorTreaties.title: Honor Treaties
relations.i.honorTreaties.label: The Quran commands fulfilling treaties with those who have not broken them.
relations.i.breakTreaty.title: Respond to Treaty Breaking
relations.i.breakTreaty.label: The Quran allows ending a treaty with those who break it.
relations.i.refugeSeeker.title: Grant Refuge to One Who Seeks It
relations.i.refugeSeeker.label: The Quran commands granting protection to a disbeliever who seeks refuge.
brotherhood.title: Brotherhood & Community
brotherhood.subtitle: Quranic references on Muslim unity, reconciliation, cooperation, and the ummah.
brotherhood.sourceNote: Brotherhood references are shown from direct Quran ayahs only. No generated commentary.
brotherhood.i.believersBrothers.title: Believers Are Brothers
brotherhood.i.believersBrothers.label: The Quran declares all believers are brothers and commands reconciliation.
brotherhood.i.holdRope.title: Hold to Allah's Rope Together
brotherhood.i.holdRope.label: The Quran commands holding to the rope of Allah all together and not dividing.
brotherhood.i.doNotDivide.title: Do Not Divide
brotherhood.i.doNotDivide.label: The Quran condemns dividing into sects after clear guidance has come.
brotherhood.i.reconcileDispute.title: Reconcile Those in Dispute
brotherhood.i.reconcileDispute.label: The Quran commands making peace between two disputing groups of believers.
brotherhood.i.makeSettlement.title: Settlement Is Better
brotherhood.i.makeSettlement.label: The Quran favors reconciliation and settlement over prolonged dispute.
brotherhood.i.cooperateGood.title: Cooperate in Goodness
brotherhood.i.cooperateGood.label: The Quran commands cooperating in righteousness and taqwa, not in sin.
brotherhood.i.forbidEvil.title: Forbid Evil Together
brotherhood.i.forbidEvil.label: The Quran calls believers to command good and forbid evil together.
brotherhood.i.noEnmity.title: No Enmity Among Believers
brotherhood.i.noEnmity.label: The Quran forbids enmity between believers and asks forgiveness for all.
brotherhood.i.community.title: Best Community
brotherhood.i.community.label: The Quran describes the Muslim community as the best brought forth for mankind.
oaths.title: Oaths, Vows & Expiation
oaths.subtitle: Quranic references on oaths, their expiation, zihar, ila, and fulfilling vows.
oaths.sourceNote: Oaths references are shown from direct Quran ayahs only. Legal application requires qualified scholarship.
oaths.i.doNotMakeObstacle.title: Do Not Make Oaths an Obstacle
oaths.i.doNotMakeObstacle.label: The Quran warns against using Allah's name as an excuse to avoid doing good.
oaths.i.laghwOath.title: Unintentional Oaths Overlooked
oaths.i.laghwOath.label: The Quran distinguishes unintentional oaths from deliberate ones.
oaths.i.oathExpiation.title: Expiation for Oaths
oaths.i.oathExpiation.label: The Quran prescribes expiation for breaking a deliberate oath.
oaths.i.expiateFeed.title: Feed Ten Poor People
oaths.i.expiateFeed.label: One form of expiation for oaths is feeding or clothing ten poor people.
oaths.i.expiateFasting.title: Fasting as Expiation
oaths.i.expiateFasting.label: If unable to do other expiation, fasting three days is prescribed.
oaths.i.ila.title: Ila — Oath of Abstention
oaths.i.ila.label: The Quran gives a four-month period for those who take an oath to abstain.
oaths.i.zihar.title: Zihar — Unlawful Comparison
oaths.i.zihar.label: The Quran addresses zihar and calls it an evil statement.
oaths.i.ziharExpiation.title: Expiation for Zihar
oaths.i.ziharExpiation.label: The Quran prescribes freeing a slave, fasting, or feeding the poor for zihar.
oaths.i.fulfillVows.title: Fulfill Vows
oaths.i.fulfillVows.label: The Quran praises those who fulfill their vows and commands fulfilling them.
